title: Test suite catalog
description: Classification of Forge test suites: what each one needs to run and what its fixture actually proves. Only suites listed in the catalog are classified; everything else in test/ is explicitly unclassified.

schemaVersion.description: Incremented when a change to this schema breaks existing readers.

scope.description: What this catalog covers and what it deliberately does not.

classified.description: Human-readable list of the areas that are classified.

unclassified.description: Statement of what is left unclassified and how to treat it.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the catalog.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the test file; must exist.

contracts.description: Test contracts defined in the file.

fixture.description: What the fixture builds, and therefore what a pass is evidence for. local-deployment: everything deployed in the test. fork-fresh-deployment: fork state, but the contract under test is deployed by the fixture. fork-upgrade: an existing proxy on a fork is deliberately upgraded or reconfigured. deployed-usage: an existing deployment is used unchanged, without upgrade, code replacement or self-granted roles.

profile.description: Foundry profile the suite is run under.

rpc.description: Name of the provider environment variable the suite reads, or null when it needs no RPC. Never a URL.

block.description: Pinned fork block, or null when the suite does not fork.

ffi.description: Whether the suite calls vm.ffi. This records actual use; the selected pilot profiles deny FFI when it is false.

tests.description: Number of test functions the suite ran when it was last classified.

setUp.description: What setUp() and its helpers build before the first test runs.

mutations.description: Cheatcode-driven changes to state the fixture did not create: pranks, role grants, dealt balances, upgrades.

externalAddresses.description: Hardcoded on-chain addresses the fixture reads or impersonates, with the role each plays.

helpers.description: Shared helper libraries or base contracts the fixture pulls in.
